QF.id: Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_19

question.text: An Interval Fund combines features of which two types of fund structures?

explanation.text: The Logic: An Interval Fund is a unique structure that combines features of both open-ended and close-ended funds. It remains close-ended for most of the time (units cannot be redeemed) but opens at specified intervals (called "transaction periods") for purchase and redemption at NAV. These transaction periods must be at least 2 days and the minimum gap between two transaction periods must be 15 days. The fund must be listed on an exchange for liquidity between intervals. The Trap: The question asks about fund STRUCTURE classification, not investment classification. Options B, C, and D describe investment-related combinations (asset type, geography, management style), not structural features. A hybrid fund combines equity and debt (investment classification), while an interval fund combines open-ended and close-ended features (structural classification). This distinction between classification dimensions is key.
